summary.text: Amish Shah is an emergency-medicine physician and the Democratic nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District, an open seat. He served in the Arizona House of Representatives from 2019 to 2024 and was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024, losing to Rep. David Schweikert. His campaign website says he has focused on teacher pay, small businesses, and public health and safety.

paragraphs.text: Shah was born in Chicago, Illinois, and was raised there by immigrant parents from India, according to FOX 10 Phoenix.

He earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Northwestern University in 1997, an M.D. from Northwestern in 2001, and a master's in public health from the University of California, Berkeley in 2003.

His career experience includes working as an attending physician with Mayo Clinic, Dignity Health, and IASIS Healthcare, and as chief medical officer of Urgent Consult. He was an airway management physician with the New York Jets and a faculty member at Mount Sinai Medical Center, and his campaign says he is board certified in emergency medicine and continues to practice.
Shah won three consecutive elections to the Arizona House of Representatives, in 2018, 2020 and 2022, and served from 2019 to 2024, first in District 24 and, after redistricting, in District 5.
According to his campaign website, he had more bills signed into law than any Arizona Democrat in the last decade and worked across party lines.
In 2024 he won the Democratic primary for Arizona's 1st Congressional District with 23.5% of the vote, then lost the general election to incumbent Rep. David Schweikert, 51.9% to 48.1%.
Shah won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary for the open seat with 39.4% of the vote, ahead of Marlene Galan-Woods (34.4%), Jonathan Treble and Rick McCartney.
